governing_rules: Separate source-derived claims from modern or operational extensions.
Preserve current-verification flags unless official docs and project runtime have been checked.
Use reusable risk IDs instead of duplicating long warnings.
Prefer service boundaries and result contracts over top-level UI side effects.
Never treat missing chapters 8-13 as processed content.
Treat Streamlit as a UI/front-end layer, not a backend, scheduler, permission system, transaction manager, or audit ledger.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Top-to-bottom script execution
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Keep rendering deterministic; move non-idempotent work behind explicit events and service calls.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Perform database writes, emails, or remote API mutations while rendering page headers or widgets.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Rerun-centered app model
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Assume user interaction can cause script re-execution; make all top-level code safe to repeat.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Use module globals or top-level calls as if they run only once per user journey.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Widget-triggered reruns
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Separate lightweight UI recomputation from expensive/service operations; cache or guard slow reads.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Bind expensive operations directly to each widget value without a submit boundary.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Buttons as momentary triggers
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: On click, create or update explicit state such as a pending plan id or result object.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Use a button alone to mean a job remains approved across later reruns.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Forms as grouped submission boundaries
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Use a form for multi-field inputs and perform validation only after the submit button returns true.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Start live actions while the user is still editing fields inside or outside the form.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Session state as per-user UI workflow state
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Use session state for per-user, non-durable UI workflow markers; write durable results outside Streamlit.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Use session state as database, run ledger, permission system, or audit trail.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Session state initialization
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Initialize all expected UI workflow keys at page entry with safe defaults and schema comments.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Create keys lazily in scattered callbacks, or let missing keys imply permissions.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Cache data versus cache resource
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Use data cache for repeatable data transforms and resource cache for expensive shared resources only after sensitivity review.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Cache secrets, user-specific protected data, mutable results, or write clients without lifecycle checks.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Cache invalidation and refresh controls
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Tie cache keys to file hash, user scope, dataset version, and explicit refresh controls where relevant.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Use cache defaults for operational dashboards, permissioned data, or changing external systems.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Long-running operations
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Use submit boundaries, cached pure work, asynchronous backend jobs where needed, visible progress, and timeout states.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Run long calls during every render or every widget edit.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Status display
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Show plain-language status tied to actual state and backend result contracts.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Show a generic success message before validation, persistence, or backend completion.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Progress display
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Use progress only when the operation has meaningful phases or estimated completion; otherwise show bounded status and next steps.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Use fake progress to imply success or hide failures.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Exception display and user-safe errors
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Show user-safe errors with correlation/run id; log redacted technical detail outside the UI.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Call st.exception or print raw traceback for non-admin users.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Stop/rerun flow control
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Use stop-like guard clauses after blockers; use rerun APIs only with current-version checks and loop prevention.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Continue into parse/process/live action after missing file or invalid form state.

rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.name: Safe side-effect boundaries
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.safe_pattern: Route live actions through service functions after submit, dry-run, confirmation, backend authorization, idempotency key, and result contract.
rerun_side_effect_safety_rules.dangerous_pattern: Perform live writes directly in top-level app code or callbacks without a persisted plan id.

must_not_do: perform durable writes at render time

responsibilities: separate user-safe message from internal detail
must_not_do: return raw exception as user result

responsibilities: record who did what and why

dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Validate files before transformation or live use
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Streamlit collects file and displays validation; parser/service owns schema and transformation contract.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.pattern_name: inputs → form submit → dry run → confirmation → live execution
dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Prevent accidental live mutations from multi-field inputs
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Streamlit submits intent; backend service creates dry-run plan and executes only matching approved plan.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.pattern_name: live action guarded by backend authorization
dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Ensure UI affordances do not become permission enforcement
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Backend permission service decides; Streamlit only passes actor, scope, and requested operation.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.pattern_name: live action linked to a specific dry-run plan ID
dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Avoid executing a different operation than the reviewed preview
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Service creates immutable plan; Streamlit displays plan digest and submits exact id.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Make post-run outcome clear to nontechnical users
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Streamlit displays result contract; service owns final state.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Prevent all-or-nothing confusion when some rows/items fail
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Service returns row/item-level results; Streamlit groups by business meaning.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Avoid orphaned or ambiguous long operations
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Backend job runner owns cancellation semantics; Streamlit only requests and displays.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Prevent users from thinking an action changed data when it did nothing
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Service identifies no-op and warnings before live execution.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Give users a durable artifact without exposing unsafe data
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Backend/report service creates artifact; Streamlit provides download button/link.

dry_run_live_workflow_model.goal: Make prior runs reviewable without treating session state as storage
dry_run_live_workflow_model.service_boundary: Durable run ledger owns history; Streamlit queries and displays it.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can display login/logout controls and user identity only when current supported auth is configured.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Identity provider/session management must be configured and validated outside ordinary page hiding.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: A username in session state or text input proves identity.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can conditionally render controls after receiving an authorization result.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Permission decisions for live actions must be enforced in backend services/adapters.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: A hidden page, disabled button, or route omission is authorization.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can show current role/scope labels and filter UI choices.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Role and scope claims must come from trusted identity/permissions systems.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can collect company, location, workflow, or tenant selection.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Tenant/resource permissions must be checked by services for every query and action.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: Filtering a selectbox is enough to prevent cross-tenant access.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Chapter 5 demonstrates st.secrets for deployed apps; current behavior must be checked.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Secret lifecycle, rotation, least privilege, and CI/CD injection must be enforced by platform/process.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: Putting secrets in code, session state, cache, or repo is acceptable for convenience.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can render redacted placeholders and connection status.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Actual secret values must never be revealed to ordinary users or included in client-delivered artifacts.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: Admin dashboard can print tokens for debugging.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can show user-friendly errors and admin-only details if properly gated.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Logging/redaction/correlation ids must be managed outside the UI.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: Raw exceptions are fine because Streamlit users are trusted.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can provide downloads for reports or transformed data.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Authorization, redaction, retention, artifact integrity, and data classification must be enforced outside UI widgets.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: Download button is safe because the user can see the page.

security_auth_secrets_rules.what_streamlit_can_do: Streamlit can display selected operational summaries.
security_auth_secrets_rules.what_must_be_enforced_outside_streamlit: Central logs, audit ledger, and redaction filters must be outside Streamlit rendering code.
security_auth_secrets_rules.dangerous_assumption: Printing inputs/exceptions is harmless during app operation.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Use direct status labels tied to real result state and next action.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Show spinner/green check without business meaning.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Show what changed, which records are affected, and what action is safe before logs/details.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Lead with dataframe dumps, JSON, or exceptions.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Show required basics first; reveal advanced/debug sections only when relevant.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Put admin, debug, and live controls beside first-step upload controls.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Display filename, size, detected type, hash/preview, and validation status before processing.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Let the Process button remain ambiguous after selecting a new file.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Disable or hide live controls until validation, dry-run, authorization, and confirmation are satisfied; still enforce server-side.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Use disabled button as the only safety mechanism.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Use confirmation copy that names scope, count, target, and irreversibility; require exact plan match for live action.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Generic “Are you sure?” near a mutable plan.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Separate blockers from warnings and make live behavior explicit.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Mix all issues in one red error list.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Show totals, successful items, failed items, warning groups, and next steps.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Display a single success toast for partial completion.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Show last refresh time, source, filters, completeness, and manual refresh affordance.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Cache a dashboard with no freshness label.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Show KPI, risk, freshness, exception count, and recommended next action.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Show only charts without caveats or data definitions.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Use period/entity selectors, file hash, row count, totals, reconciliation warnings, and exportable validation report.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Process financial rows after upload with no totals or period confirmation.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Use step-by-step pages, clear blockers, examples, and safe defaults.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Expose developer controls and raw technical failures.

nontechnical_user_ux_rules.recommended_ui_behavior: Centralize labels/messages and keep business meaning separate from code identifiers.
nontechnical_user_ux_rules.bad_ui_behavior: Intermix English UI copy in validation/business logic.

testing_observability_rules.risk_addressed: UI/business logic coupling and untestable live behavior
Bad inputs reaching processing or live actions
Parser errors, unsafe file assumptions, and bad previews
Live execution differs from reviewed plan
Repeated click or refresh causes duplicate live action
Batch partial failures shown as success or raw errors
Long operations hang or rerun indefinitely
Secrets leak in UI, logs, downloads, cache, or exceptions
Assuming unavailable or changed Streamlit test APIs

recommended_upload_strategy: Display visible file state and preview.
Process only a validated file hash.
Return result contract and downloadable redacted report.

risk_summaries.risk_description: A write, API call, email, or job launch happens during normal top-to-bottom rendering rather than behind an explicit submit/confirmation/service boundary.
A user rerun, browser refresh, impatient click, or retry can perform the same live action more than once.
Per-user UI state is treated as durable storage, audit history, queue, or database.
A value in session state is treated as proof that a user may perform an action.
Hiding a page, widget, or button is mistaken for permission enforcement.
Cached values are reused after inputs, files, permissions, or external data changed.
Secrets, tokens, user-specific private data, or restricted results are cached without isolation and redaction controls.
A cached object is mutated and then leaks stale or cross-request state into later runs.
Uploaded file content is parsed or processed before extension, size, schema, type, and business-rule validation.
A destructive, financial, database, or API write occurs without preview, dry-run plan, confirmation, and backend authorization.
A slow model, file parse, API call, or report generation repeats on normal widget changes.
Tracebacks, credentials, SQL, tokens, file paths, or internal details are shown to ordinary users.
Credentials appear in code, logs, UI, downloaded files, exceptions, cache entries, or committed repositories.
An executive/owner dashboard displays success while data is stale, partial, filtered, failed, or unvalidated.
Core rules live in Streamlit rendering code, making rerun behavior, tests, and service reuse unsafe.
The app is treated as the durable job engine, scheduler, auth server, transaction manager, or audit ledger.
A current Streamlit API, component, Cloud behavior, auth option, or testing tool is assumed without checking the installed version and official docs.

script_execution: chapter 1 demonstrates Streamlit apps as Python scripts and top-to-bottom rendering with visible changes after saving/rerunning
widgets: chapters 1, 2, 4, 6 demonstrate button, selectbox, slider, number_input, text_input, color_picker, sidebar, tabs, columns, and multipage layout
forms: chapter 4 demonstrates st.form and st.form_submit_button around grouped ML inputs
file_workflows: chapter 2 demonstrates st.file_uploader, CSV reads with pandas, st.stop when no file is present, and download behavior
caching: chapter 2 demonstrates st.cache_data for data loading; chapter 4 demonstrates st.cache_resource for a model resource
visualization: chapter 3 demonstrates Streamlit charts and third-party visualization libraries
deployment: chapter 5 demonstrates GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud deployment and st.secrets usage
components: chapter 7 demonstrates selected community components; these should not be treated as stable/current without verification
